critical_code_review_comments: server.py L298-301: honeypot path creates a dummy ContactSubmission with a real uuid id and current timestamp before returning it. Since it's excluded from DB, this is fine, but the ID/created_at leak that the endpoint accepted the payload. Consider returning static/opaque dummy values to avoid confirming successful shape to bots.

contact_rate_check keys purely by IP; behind NAT/CGNAT (mobile carriers, offices) legitimate users share IPs. 10/hr per IP may falsely rate-limit real users. Acceptable for a demo site; for production consider IP+email OR captcha as secondary signal.

client_ip() derivation via TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS from the RIGHT of X-Forwarded-For is correct for a single trusted ingress; document TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS in .env.example so ops knows to bump it if hops change (currently defaults to 1).

TTL index on contact_events.ts uses expireAfterSeconds=86400 (24h) which is fine for a 1h window rate limit. daily_send_allowed() reuses same collection to count today's ALL events (including from other IPs) as email dispatch cap - correct but note this couples the two mechanisms; if you ever raise per-IP limit above the daily cap the daily cap becomes the binding constraint silently.
_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH still generated once at import (unchanged from prior review) - rotating ADMIN_PASSWORD requires backend restart.

Honeypot check uses payload.website.strip() so whitespace-only submissions still pass to the real path. Fine because Pydantic still validates the other fields, but a bot could send '   ' as website and be treated as legitimate; minor.
